content: 1. The STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) statement provides detailed guidelines for reporting observational studies, ensuring clarity and transparency in study design, methodology, and findings. It was published in PLoS Medicine in 2007. 2. MiraTes-Europe BV emphasized the importance of HIV home testing as a critical strategy to reach high-risk populations. This approach was highlighted in their 2008 report. 3. Ochako R, Vu L, and Peterson K conducted a study in Kenya to understand the potential users and effective messaging for HIV oral self-test kits. Their findings were documented in the 2014 3ie Grantee Final Report. 4. Katz D, Golden M, Hughes J, Farquhar C, and Steckler J presented research on the acceptability and ease of use of home self-testing for HIV among men who have sex with men (MSM) at the 2012 Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in Seattle. 5. Hopewell S, Clarke M, Moher D, Wager E, Middleton P, Altman DG, and colleagues elaborated on the CONSORT (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials) guidelines for reporting randomized controlled trials in journals and conference abstracts. This was published in PLoS Medicine in 2008. 6. Carballo-Diéguez A, Frasca T, Balan I, Ibitoye M, and Dolezal C demonstrated that the use of rapid HIV home tests can prevent HIV exposure in high-risk MSM populations. Their findings were published in AIDS and Behavior in 2012. 7. Carballo-Diéguez A, Frasca T, Dolezal C, and Balan I explored whether gay and bisexual men at high risk of HIV infection would use over-the-counter rapid HIV tests to screen sexual partners. This study was published in the Journal of Sex Research in 2012. 8. Gray RT, Prestage GP, Down I, Ghaus MH, Hoare A, Bradley J, and colleagues analyzed the impact of increased HIV testing on reducing HIV incidence among gay men in New South Wales. Their study, published in PLoS One in 2013, highlighted the acceptability of convenient HIV testing methods. 9. Marley G, Kang D, Wilson E, Huang T, Qian Y, Li X, and colleagues introduced rapid oral-fluid HIV testing among high-risk populations in Shandong, China. They discussed the feasibility and challenges in their 2014 study published in BMC Public Health. 10. Attree P and Milton B critically appraised qualitative research for systematic reviews, addressing methodological challenges. Their work was published in Evidence & Policy in 2006. 11. Bavinton BR, Brown G, Hurley M, Bradley J, Keen P, Conway DP, and colleagues investigated which gay men would increase their frequency of HIV testing with home self-testing. Their findings were published in AIDS and Behavior in 2013. 12. Bilardi JE, Walker S, Read T, Prestage G, Chen MY, Guy R, and colleagues explored gay and bisexual men's views on rapid self-testing for HIV. Their study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2013. 13. Chen MY, Bilardi JE, Lee D, Cummings RC, Bush M, Fairley CK, and colleagues found that Australian MSM preferred rapid oral HIV testing over conventional blood testing. This study was published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2010. 14. De la Fuente L, Rosales-Statkus ME, Hoyos J, Pulido J, Santos S, Bravo MJ, and colleagues assessed whether participants in a street-based HIV testing program could perform and interpret their own rapid tests. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2012. 15. Greacen T, Friboulet D, Blachier A, Fugon L, Hefez S, Lorente N, and colleagues found that internet-using MSM were interested in accessing authorized HIV self-tests available for online purchase. This study was published in AIDS Care in 2013. 16. Han L, Bien CH, Wei C, Muessig KE, Yang M, Liu F, and colleagues examined HIV self-testing among online MSM in China and its implications for expanding HIV testing among key populations. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2014. 17. Lee VJ, Tan SC, Earnest A, Seong PS, Tan HH, Leo YS, and colleagues evaluated the user acceptability and feasibility of self-testing with HIV rapid tests. Their study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2007. 18. Lippman SA, Périssé ARS, Veloso VG, Sullivan PS, Buchbinder S, Sineath RC, and colleagues assessed the acceptability of self-conducted home-based HIV testing among MSM in Brazil through an online survey. Their findings were published in Cadernos de Saúde Pública in 2014. 19. Ng OT, Chow AL, Lee VJ, Chen MIC, Win MK, Tan HH, and colleagues evaluated the accuracy and user acceptability of HIV self-testing using an oral fluid-based rapid test. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2012. 20. Skolnik HS, Phillips KA, Binson D, and Dilley JW explored factors influencing decisions on where and how to be tested for HIV. Their study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2001. 21. Spielberg F, Branson BM, Goldbaum GM, Lockhart D, Kurth A, Celum CL, and colleagues investigated preferences for new HIV testing strategies among clients of needle exchange programs, STD clinics, and sex venues for MSM. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2003. 22. Xun H, Kang D, Huang T, Qian Y, Li X, Wilson EC, and colleagues identified factors associated with the willingness to accept oral fluid HIV rapid testing among high-risk populations in China. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2013. 23. Bavinton B, Grulich A, Keen P, Zablotska I, Murphy D, Brown G, and colleagues explored motivations for and implications of using home HIV tests among Australian gay men. Their findings were presented at the 2014 International AIDS Conference in Melbourne. 24. Chakravarty D, Darbes L, Neilands T, Beougher S, Finlayson S, and Hoff C examined attitudes about rapid, over-the-counter HIV home-testing kits among MSM couples. Their findings were presented at the 2014 International AIDS Conference in Melbourne. 25. Mayer K, Tomassilli J, Gelman M, Altfeld M, and Allen T evaluated the acceptability of biweekly finger pricks for HIV self-testing among MSM using the Alere Determine™ HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab assay. Their findings were presented at the 2014 International AIDS Conference in Melbourne. 26. Wong HTH and Lee SS studied patterns of in-home self-testing for HIV among an internet sample of MSM in an Asian population. Their findings were presented at the 2014 International AIDS Conference in Melbourne. 27. Han X, Xu J, Chu Z, Dai D, Lu C, Wang X, and colleagues screened for acute HIV infections among Chinese MSM at voluntary counseling and testing centers. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2011. 28. Gaydos CA, Hsieh YH, Harvey L, Burah A, Won H, Jett-Goheen M, and colleagues investigated whether patients would opt to perform their own rapid HIV test in the emergency department. Their study was published in Annals of Emergency Medicine in 2011. 29. Peck R, Lim J, van Rooyen H, Mukoma W, Chepuka L, Bansil P, and colleagues conducted a usability study of HIV self-test prototypes in Kenya, Malawi, and South Africa to determine the ideal design for unsupervised self-testing. Their findings were published in AIDS and Behavior in 2014. 30. Dong K, Regina R, Hlongwane S, Ghebremichael M, Wilson D, and Dong K assessed whether laypersons in high-prevalence South Africa could accurately perform an HIV self-test. Their findings were presented at the 2014 International AIDS Conference in Melbourne. 31. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provided a summary of the safety and effectiveness of the OraQuick® In-Home HIV Test in 2012. 32. OraSure Technologies provided information on the OraQuick® HIV self-test on their website in 2014. 33. Curran K, Johnson C, Ngure K, Mugo N, Baeten J, Heffron R, and colleagues explored the potential role of HIV self-testing within pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) implementation. Their findings were presented at the 2014 International AIDS Conference in Melbourne. 34. MacPherson P, Lalloo DG, Webb EL, and colleagues evaluated the effect of optional home initiation of HIV care following self-testing on antiretroviral therapy initiation among adults in Malawi. Their randomized clinical trial was published in JAMA in 2014. 35. Brown A, Djimeu E, and Cameron D reviewed evidence of harm from self-tests, with their findings published in AIDS and Behavior in 2014.
